You review lifestyle plans written by FOXO's lifestyle coach for a member in India.

You will see the member's profile, the abnormal results the plan targets, and the full plan. Judge whether a member could act on the plan tomorrow. Do not judge medical correctness here; other checks cover that.

For each criterion, first write one or two sentences of reasoning, then set passed to true or false.

Criteria (use these ids exactly, one entry each):
- specific: Recommendations give concrete foods with portions or timing, not generic advice like "eat healthy".
- practical: The foods are everyday Indian foods a member could easily buy and cook.
- explained: Each recommendation says how it helps the linked biomarker.
- activity_concrete: The activity advice says what to do, for how long and how often.

Respond with a single JSON object that matches this JSON schema:
{"$defs": {"CriterionVerdict": {"properties": {"criterion": {"title": "Criterion", "type": "string"}, "reasoning": {"title": "Reasoning", "type": "string"}, "passed": {"title": "Passed", "type": "boolean"}}, "required": ["criterion", "reasoning", "passed"], "title": "CriterionVerdict", "type": "object"}}, "properties": {"criteria": {"items": {"$ref": "#/$defs/CriterionVerdict"}, "title": "Criteria", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["criteria"], "title": "JudgeOutput", "type": "object"}

Diet: eggetarian. Allergies: peanut. Conditions: none.
Abnormal results: ldl 162.0 mg/dL (high), hdl 36.0 mg/dL (low)

Plan:
Focus areas: Bringing down high LDL cholesterol (162 mg/dL) with more soluble fibre and better fats; Raising low HDL cholesterol (36 mg/dL) with regular activity, nuts and seeds; Strictly avoiding peanuts and all peanut-containing foods (allergy); Replacing deep-fried and refined snacks with home-cooked eggetarian meals built on dal, millets and seasonal sabzi
Foods to eat:
- Breakfast (within 1 hour of waking): 1 bowl of porridge made from 40 g dry rolled oats or 2 tbsp barley dalia cooked in 150 ml toned milk, topped with 1 chopped apple or half a guava. On alternate days, have 2 moong dal chillas with mint-coriander chutney (check it has no peanuts) instead. (why: Oats and barley are rich in beta-glucan, a soluble fibre that binds cholesterol in the gut and lowers LDL. Replacing a refined breakfast with this also cuts maida and butter.; linked to ldl)
- Lunch and dinner: 1 katori (about 150 g cooked) of any whole legume every day - rajma, kala chana, lobia, whole moong or chana dal - along with 1 roti made of bajra, jowar or ragi instead of white rice or maida roti. Keep rice to 1 small katori if you want it. (why: Legumes and millets supply soluble and insoluble fibre that lowers LDL and keeps you full, so you eat less fried food. Millets replace refined grains that push LDL up.; linked to ldl)
- Mid-morning snack (around 11 am): 6-8 whole unsalted almonds plus 2 walnut halves (about 30 g total), or 1 tbsp ground flaxseed (alsi) mixed into curd. Buy plain nuts and check the packet label - no peanuts, no peanut oil, no 'may contain peanuts' products. (why: Almonds, walnuts and flaxseed give polyunsaturated fats and plant omega-3 that help raise HDL. Your peanut allergy means all nut intake must come from non-peanut sources only.; linked to hdl)
- Cooking fat: use only 3-4 teaspoons of oil per person per day - mustard oil, rice bran oil or olive oil. Measure with a spoon, do not pour from the bottle. Avoid groundnut (peanut) oil completely. (why: Most people with high LDL take far too much cooking fat, and ghee/butter/coconut oil are high in saturated fat. Shifting to measured unsaturated oils lowers LDL. Groundnut oil is excluded because of your peanut allergy.; linked to ldl)
- Protein at meals: 3-4 whole eggs per week (boiled, or as bhurji with 1 teaspoon oil) and egg whites freely - up to 4-5 whites a week in an omelette or boiled. Pair with 1 katori dal at lunch and dinner. Do not deep-fry eggs in oil. (why: Eggs are a good eggetarian protein that replaces fried snacks and refined carbs in the diet, which supports healthier HDL levels. Keeping whole eggs to 3-4 a week limits dietary cholesterol while you bring LDL down.; linked to hdl)
- Vegetables and fruit: 3 katori of seasonal sabzi daily (bhindi, lauki, palak, methi, beans, cabbage, gourds) and 2 whole fruits - guava, apple, orange or papaya - one at 5 pm instead of tea-time biscuits. (why: Fruit pectin and vegetable fibre increase soluble fibre intake, which lowers LDL, and the 5 pm fruit swap removes fried namkeen and bakery snacks.; linked to ldl)
- Evening meal timing: finish dinner by 8-8:30 pm, at least 2-3 hours before sleeping. Keep dinner light - 1 katori dal, 1 millet roti, 1 katori sabzi and a small bowl of curd. (why: An early, light dinner reduces late-night snacking on fried and sweet foods, which is one of the main drivers of high LDL and low HDL in Indian diets.; linked to ldl)
Foods to limit or avoid: Peanuts in every form - roasted peanuts, peanut chikki, peanut chutney, groundnut oil, satay-style sauces and any packaged food labelled 'may contain peanuts' (allergy); Deep-fried foods - samosa, pakora, puri, bhatura, vada, papad fried in oil, french fries and fried namkeen; Ghee, butter, coconut oil, vanaspati and bakery items made with them - croissants, puffs, biscuits, cakes, rusk; Whole milk, malai, cream-based gravies and large amounts of full-fat paneer; use toned milk and limited paneer; Sweets, mithai, jaggery-based items, sweetened drinks, packaged juices and soft drinks; Large portions of white rice, maida roti, white bread and instant noodles
Activity: Your doctor has not restricted exercise, so aim for a brisk 35-40 minute walk 5 days a week (morning or evening, at a pace where you can talk but not sing), plus 2 days a week of simple strength work at home - 2 sets of 10 squats, 10 wall push-ups and 30-second plank. Add a 5-minute walk after each main meal. Build up gradually, and if you feel chest pain, breathlessness or dizziness, stop and follow your doctor's advice.
Sleep: Sleep 7-8 hours every night with a fixed sleep and wake time - lights out by 11 pm and up by 6:30-7 am. Keep screens off for 30 minutes before bed, and avoid tea or coffee after 5 pm.
Retest in 12 weeks
